patterns.title: Map request and failure boundaries
patterns.problem: Unclear service ownership hides failure behavior.
patterns.when_to_use: Before adding a new backend path.
patterns.approach: Trace authorization, validation, service, transaction/queue and result; assign data ownership and define each failure response.
verification: Trace a successful request and a timeout at each boundary.

patterns.title: Select the simplest execution model
patterns.problem: An orchestrator is added without a recovery requirement.
patterns.when_to_use: Choosing synchronous, queued, agentic or durable execution.
patterns.approach: Start with a bounded request or job; use a graph for branching state, a durable orchestrator for durable waits, and a DAG for partition dependencies.
verification: Explain which crash/wait requirement the selected mechanism satisfies.

patterns.title: Commit state and publication with an outbox
patterns.problem: A write succeeds but its required event is never published.
patterns.when_to_use: A domain change and eventual publication must both persist.
patterns.approach: Write domain state and an outbox entry in one transaction; publish with retries and deduplicate consumers using stable event IDs.
verification: Crash between commit and publish; verify eventual event and one business effect.

patterns.title: Bound concurrency and dependency capacity
patterns.problem: Retrying workers consume shared pools and overload dependencies.
patterns.when_to_use: Sizing API replicas, job workers and database pools.
patterns.approach: Budget total connections and inflight work across replicas; enforce queue/concurrency limits, deadlines and an explicit overload response.
verification: Load with an unavailable dependency and inspect capacity, errors and queue age.

patterns.title: Define graph state and reducers
patterns.problem: Parallel nodes overwrite or duplicate shared state.
patterns.when_to_use: An agent graph has branches updating shared fields.
patterns.approach: Use typed partial updates and explicit reducers; define append, replace and deduplication semantics with stable event identity.
verification: Exercise concurrent branches and repeated updates with expected merged state.

patterns.title: Check Command routes and static edges
patterns.problem: A node executes two successors unexpectedly.
patterns.when_to_use: A LangGraph node returns Command goto while having static outgoing edges.
patterns.approach: Inspect all outgoing routes; do not assume dynamic goto cancels static edges. Test each branch and termination against the installed version.
verification: Assert the exact executed node sequence for each transition.

patterns.title: Checkpoint recovery uses stable identity
patterns.problem: Agent progress is lost on restart or exposed by a run identifier.
patterns.when_to_use: An agent must resume after process loss.
patterns.approach: Persist checkpoints under stable run identity, authorize their access from tenant context, and keep cross-run memory separate with retention rules.
verification: Restart after a persisted transition and test another tenant accessing the run.

patterns.title: Reconcile external effects before retry
patterns.problem: An agent repeats a successful charge after losing its receipt.
patterns.when_to_use: An external tool effect must survive duplicate delivery or crash recovery.
patterns.approach: Persist a stable operation key; use provider idempotency or query/reconcile existing outcome before retry. Record its scope and retention.
failure_modes: Key reused for a different operation
verification: Crash after effect before receipt; repeat delivery and confirm the business invariant.

patterns.title: Assign one retry owner and deadline
patterns.problem: Nested retries multiply attempts and delay failure.
patterns.when_to_use: A task spans clients, activities and workers.
patterns.approach: Classify errors and designate a single owner per logical boundary; account for all underlying retries within an overall attempt/time budget.
verification: Inject rate limits and permanent invalid input; inspect attempts and terminal state.

patterns.title: Keep durable workflow replay deterministic
patterns.problem: Old workflow histories diverge after a deployment.
patterns.when_to_use: Temporal workflow code or dependencies change.
patterns.approach: Keep effects/model calls in activities, use replay-safe primitives, and apply supported versioning/routing while old histories remain active.
verification: Replay old histories and restart during an activity timeout.

patterns.title: Publish validated partition outputs atomically
patterns.problem: Partial files or tables become visible as complete output.
patterns.when_to_use: A batch task materializes a data partition.
patterns.approach: Write to staging, validate checksum/schema/invariants, then publish atomically where supported; pass artifact references between tasks.
verification: Terminate during write and verify consumers see only complete published output.

patterns.title: Define overlapping backfill semantics
patterns.problem: A historical rerun conflicts with the scheduled run.
patterns.when_to_use: Backfilling event-time partitions.
patterns.approach: Define timezone, watermark, late-data handling, merge keys and publication ownership; bound concurrency and make overlap deterministic or excluded.
verification: Repeat and overlap the same partition and check row/artifact invariants.

patterns.title: Compare algorithms with a trusted small-input oracle
patterns.problem: An optimized algorithm produces plausible but wrong answers.
patterns.when_to_use: Implementing or replacing a nontrivial algorithm.
patterns.approach: Write a straightforward oracle and compare generated/adversarial small cases; define ties, invalid inputs and numeric tolerances.
verification: Cover empty, duplicate, extreme and skewed inputs with independent expected outcomes.

patterns.title: Account for remote calls in complexity
patterns.problem: A nominally linear routine performs one database call per item.
patterns.when_to_use: Analyzing backend algorithm cost.
patterns.approach: Name input/workload dimensions and time/space cost; include remote round trips, critical path, allocation and batching opportunities.
verification: Count queries/calls and measure representative large inputs.

patterns.title: Profile before optimizing
patterns.problem: A change improves a microbenchmark but hurts real workloads.
patterns.when_to_use: Performance acceptance is unmet.
patterns.approach: Capture representative baseline data and environment, profile the limiting mechanism, change one bottleneck and compare equal workloads.
failure_modes: Regression in memory or p95 latency
verification: Repeat measurements and report latency distribution, throughput, memory and error rate as relevant.

patterns.title: Bound asynchronous work and cancellation
patterns.problem: Async work creates too many tasks or survives cancelled requests.
patterns.when_to_use: Parallel I/O or CPU jobs are introduced.
patterns.approach: Limit inflight work and queues, propagate deadlines/cancellation, and select CPU parallelism based on actual runtime/workload.
verification: Test cancellation and overload; confirm no orphan tasks and bounded resource use.

patterns.title: Enforce race-safe uniqueness in the database
patterns.problem: Concurrent requests both pass read-before-write validation.
patterns.when_to_use: Creating records or deduplicating operation keys.
patterns.approach: Add the appropriate unique/check/foreign-key constraints and use atomic insert/upsert semantics; define conflict results.
verification: Issue simultaneous equivalent writes and assert the committed invariant.

patterns.title: Keep external work outside lock-holding transactions
patterns.problem: A slow model or HTTP request blocks database writers.
patterns.when_to_use: A transaction crosses an external dependency.
patterns.approach: Persist a pending state or outbox, commit promptly, execute external work separately, and transition with race-safe validation.
verification: Delay the dependency and verify other transactions and recovery remain viable.

patterns.title: Use realistic query plans before adding indexes
patterns.problem: Indexes are chosen from intuition or empty development tables.
patterns.when_to_use: A database query degrades under representative load.
patterns.approach: Inspect EXPLAIN and cardinality, match predicates/order/selectivity, and account for write/storage cost; ANALYZE executes the query including writes.
verification: Compare realistic plans and runtime in a safe environment; allow justified sequential scans.

patterns.title: Migrate with compatible expand and contract stages
patterns.problem: Old application workers break during a schema change.
patterns.when_to_use: Deploying a compatibility-sensitive migration.
patterns.approach: Expand schema, deploy compatible code, backfill in bounded restartable batches, verify invariants and retire old consumers before contraction.
verification: Test old/new compatibility and restart a failed batch with restore/recovery instructions.

patterns.title: Authorize resources from authenticated tenant context
patterns.problem: A caller accesses another tenant by knowing its object ID.
patterns.when_to_use: APIs, jobs, checkpoints or tools expose tenant data.
patterns.approach: Derive identity from verified context and enforce resource/action authorization on every entry path; test actual application database roles.
verification: Attempt cross-tenant reads/writes and forged tenant inputs.

patterns.title: Enforce tool authority outside model output
patterns.problem: Retrieved text or model arguments expand a tool permission.
patterns.when_to_use: Agents execute sensitive tools.
patterns.approach: Use typed allowlisted actions, validation, scoped credentials and code-level authorization; untrusted content cannot grant permissions.
verification: Feed adversarial retrieved instructions and forged tool arguments; confirm authority does not expand.

patterns.title: Validate signatures and duplicate callbacks
patterns.problem: A replayed or forged callback repeats a business action.
patterns.when_to_use: Receiving provider webhooks.
patterns.approach: Use provider-documented signature and replay validation, validate state/schema, and deduplicate stable event IDs before effects.
verification: Exercise invalid signatures, old callbacks, duplicates and out-of-order state transitions.

patterns.title: Protect secrets and persisted model data
patterns.problem: Prompts, checkpoints or logs retain sensitive data unexpectedly.
patterns.when_to_use: Persisting workflow/model state and operational diagnostics.
patterns.approach: Keep credentials outside serialized state, redact logs, scope access, and define rotation, retention/deletion and abuse limits.
verification: Inspect logs/checkpoints/evidence and test access, deletion and budget exhaustion.

patterns.title: Verify contract failure boundaries
patterns.problem: Unit mocks pass while integration recovery fails.
patterns.when_to_use: Selecting backend acceptance tests.
patterns.approach: Map each invariant to unit/integration/recovery evidence; cover acknowledgement, retries, isolation, restart and resource bounds as relevant.
failure_modes: Unexecuted test plan mistaken for result
verification: Run checks and retain exact commands, outputs, exit codes and revision identity.

patterns.title: Bind work evidence to the current source
patterns.problem: A stale plan receipt causes repeated or wrong implementation.
patterns.when_to_use: Resuming a multi-step backend task.
patterns.approach: Record exact accepted source path/hash and unit coverage; compare receipt with current files before resuming or claiming completion.
verification: Rehash source and inspect owned artifacts, not worker assertions alone.

patterns.title: Review requirements and implementation independently
patterns.problem: An author misses a correctness or security assumption.
patterns.when_to_use: Completing substantial backend changes.
patterns.approach: Give a fresh reviewer exact requirements, changed scope and evidence; verify findings against code and fix acceptance blockers.
verification: Record reviewer outcomes and confirm relevant tests after fixes.

patterns.title: Treat receipt validation as a consistency check
patterns.problem: A valid receipt is presented as proof of production correctness.
patterns.when_to_use: Using the bundled completion checker.
patterns.approach: Check source digest, artifact existence, required results and blockers; independently execute tests and inspect external targets because local evidence is caller-supplied.
verification: Reject malformed/incomplete receipts and document what was actually observed.

patterns.title: Keep canonical integration with one controller
patterns.problem: Parallel workers overwrite or commit shared state.
patterns.when_to_use: Delegating independent backend units.
patterns.approach: Assign disjoint owned files/interfaces; root inspects reports and owns shared integration, final checks and canonical commits.
verification: Inspect final diff/status and stage only task-owned files.

patterns.title: Verify the requested delivery destination
patterns.problem: A local result is reported as a published PR or rollout.
patterns.when_to_use: Finishing local, PR or deployment work.
patterns.approach: Check actual destination state and relevant revision checks; no remote means honest local completion, not an invented push.
verification: Inspect created artifact or real PR/deployment and report unresolved limits.

patterns.title: Plan mixed-version rollout and recovery
patterns.problem: New code breaks active workflow histories or old schema consumers.
patterns.when_to_use: Deploying workflow/schema changes.
patterns.approach: Record revision, target, compatibility, health signals and rollback/forward recovery; rollout only within authorization.
verification: Test history/schema compatibility and meaningful operations after rollout.

patterns.title: Capture only reusable reasoning
patterns.problem: Documentation noise obscures operational lessons.
patterns.when_to_use: A solved backend failure would recur without context.
patterns.approach: Record symptom, boundary, root cause, correction, evidence and applicability when code/tests do not explain the reasoning; rebuild the knowledge index.
verification: Check source-backed canonical records and SQLite consistency.

patterns.title: Reproduce before patching
patterns.problem: Repeated speculative fixes never establish the failure.
patterns.when_to_use: A backend defect or failing check is reported.
patterns.approach: Capture expected invariant and actual request/job, minimize the reproducer, formulate a falsifiable hypothesis and verify failure before change.
verification: Show failing reproducer then passing fixed behavior and relevant regressions.

patterns.title: Trace the whole attempt history
patterns.problem: Retries hide the initial fault and duplicate effects.
patterns.when_to_use: Jobs or activities fail intermittently.
patterns.approach: Correlate operation/job/workflow IDs across attempts and acknowledgement boundaries; inspect first failure and completed effects before retrying.
verification: Inject failure between effect and acknowledgement and inspect recorded attempts.

patterns.title: Reset diagnosis after ineffective repairs
patterns.problem: A retry cap silently waives acceptance.
patterns.when_to_use: Three patches fail to improve the same symptom.
patterns.approach: Preserve evidence, revisit competing hypotheses and ownership, and report a recoverable blocked state instead of labeling failure complete.
verification: Record exact blocker, tested hypotheses and next falsifying observation.

patterns.title: Separate code fixes from existing data repair
patterns.problem: Patched code leaves historical invalid records.
patterns.when_to_use: A defect has already written corrupt state.
patterns.approach: Identify the affected set, design repeatable bounded repair, retain recovery and verify counts/invariants independently of the code fix.
verification: Repeat repair safely and check repaired and remaining records.

patterns.title: Bind requirements to executable owned units
patterns.problem: A plan lists tasks but leaves requirements or interfaces without verification.
patterns.when_to_use: Before substantial parallel or multi-unit backend execution.
patterns.approach: Assign stable requirement, unit and verification IDs; map both directions, declare interfaces and owned files, reject cycles and conflicting ownership, then inspect feasibility independently.
failure_modes: Schema pass mistaken for semantic readiness
verification: Remove a requirement link and require the structural gate to reject it.
Review actual test assertions and cross-unit interfaces.

patterns.title: Review unit spec before implementation risk
patterns.problem: Correct-looking code omits accepted behavior or reviewers inspect an obsolete snapshot.
patterns.when_to_use: Accepting delegated backend implementation units.
patterns.approach: Bind each review to current owned changes; first inspect requirement coverage, then correctness, security, recovery and test quality; repair genuine blockers and re-review the affected range.
verification: Inject an omitted requirement and require spec review to block.
Inspect fresh review coverage after a fix.

patterns.title: Observe the failing behavior proof before repair
patterns.problem: A new test passes unchanged code or fails for an unrelated setup problem.
patterns.when_to_use: Changing backend behavior, defects or behavior-changing configuration.
patterns.approach: Run the smallest meaningful invariant/boundary test, confirm its intended failure, implement the fix, observe green and refactor while retaining the oracle.
verification: Inspect the actual failure reason.
Show the old behavior fails the invariant and the repaired behavior passes.

patterns.title: Verify implementation before delivery and completion afterward
patterns.problem: A pipeline requires publication evidence before it can prepare a deliverable.
patterns.when_to_use: Nested workers returning to an autonomous backend controller.
patterns.approach: Implementation verification checks local acceptance with destination pending; the controller delivers once, then completion verification checks the observed destination and final receipt. Reuse matching current-source evidence.
failure_modes: Unit green reported as deployment success
verification: Trace the return-to-caller path with delivery pending.
Require actual destination evidence only at completion.

patterns.title: Resume the exact run from observed state
patterns.problem: Context loss restarts completed work or adopts a newer unrelated plan.
patterns.when_to_use: Continuing long backend changes or recovering interrupted workers.
patterns.approach: Reconcile accepted source digest, current files, owned commits, evidence and remote state with the ledger; preserve valid units, reopen affected checks and return the next checkpoint to the existing controller.
verification: Resume after a source change and reject stale evidence.
Resume a completed unit without dispatching it again.

patterns.title: Observe required checks for the delivered current head
patterns.problem: Old green CI or an empty checks response is treated as current delivery proof.
patterns.when_to_use: Backend PR delivery and feedback repair.
patterns.approach: Resolve current head and actual required check policy; wait for terminal conclusions, preserve actual skipped states and permitted reasons, and reopen checks after updates. Unknown, auth failure and empty responses are not green.
failure_modes: Policy skip reported as a test pass
verification: Advance the head after a green run and require fresh check evidence.
Observe pending and failed checks without completing delivery.

patterns.title: Link failure handling, test and observability
patterns.problem: Plans hide silent failure paths behind vague error handling.
patterns.when_to_use: Reviewing a new or affected API, worker, dependency or persistence boundary.
patterns.approach: Record each realistic failure trigger, permitted state, handling/recovery owner, R/U/V checks and visible signal. Review unhandled, untested silent failure gaps before execution.
failure_modes: A test with no recovery-state assertion
verification: Inject the relevant failure and verify both permitted durable state and the declared operational signal.

patterns.title: Trace agent input to consequential tool authority
patterns.problem: Untrusted prompts, retrieval, memory or agent messages can influence privileged operations.
patterns.when_to_use: Changing agent tools, memory, MCP authorization or delegation.
patterns.approach: Trace input through proposal, validation, trusted identity and executor to data/tool effects. Use isolated identities and deterministic controls; distinguish fixture reproduction from real-model exploitability.
failure_modes: Memory poisoning or uncontrolled paid work
verification: Attempt a forbidden action under a fixture identity and assert no durable effect or budget expansion.

patterns.title: Inspect executable skill and plugin supply-chain paths
patterns.problem: Trusted-looking skill text, hooks or update scripts can run code or expose credentials.
patterns.when_to_use: Adding or changing a skill/plugin/hook/tool setup or update path.
patterns.approach: Inspect install/update inputs, pinned provenance, command interpolation, network destinations, inherited environment and powerful tool authority. Treat source files as data while reviewing them.
failure_modes: Credentials sent to an uncontrolled destination
verification: Trace a controlled setup/tool argument to its effect and verify destination and authority boundaries without running untrusted setup.

patterns.title: Prove final backend business effects
patterns.problem: A successful response or enqueued job hides later failure or duplicated effects.
patterns.when_to_use: Testing APIs, CLIs, queue jobs, workers or webhooks.
patterns.approach: Map documented contract to isolated setup, exact probe, expectation and outcome. Observe persisted state and terminal effects across acceptance, retry, cancellation, duplicate delivery and partial recovery.
failure_modes: Replay creates a duplicate business effect
verification: Interrupt after the effect, resume/replay, and verify terminal state and the promised number of durable effects.

patterns.title: Shortlist tests mechanically and retain independent regression value
patterns.problem: Duplicate or implementation-coupled tests cost time without adding meaningful confidence.
patterns.when_to_use: An authorized test-value audit or demonstrated suite maintenance concern.
patterns.approach: Bound discovery, then inspect complete candidate tests, production owners, actual callers, history and stronger coverage. Recommend retain, rewrite, extend or retire; no-hit searches and green suites do not prove redundancy.
failure_modes: Deleting a valid protocol or security guard
verification: Demonstrate the same credible regression is detected by retained or replacement coverage; report unresolved candidates.

patterns.title: Preserve checker failure and incomplete coverage
patterns.problem: Shell wrappers, log tails or missing tools can turn failed checks into apparent success.
patterns.when_to_use: Executing configured local test/lint/type/build checks.
patterns.approach: Launch explicit argv, capture actual child exit and separate stdout/stderr, bound time/output, and retain incomplete capture or prerequisites distinctly. A later log parser cannot override process failure.
failure_modes: Nonzero checker exit masked by a successful tail
Timed-out or truncated evidence counted as acceptance
verification: Run controlled zero, nonzero, missing, timeout and large-output subprocesses; verify distinct truthful results and continued independent checks.

patterns.title: Observe comparable backend release baselines
patterns.problem: Deploy command success does not establish a healthy backend release.
patterns.when_to_use: A requested bounded deployment observation with available signals.
patterns.approach: Bind revision/cohort, configured thresholds, fresh windows and denominators; compare actual API/job effects and signals. Missing samples/signals remain inconclusive; use authorized recovery triggers and retain incidents.
failure_modes: Empty traffic or stale signals reported healthy
verification: Confirm deployed revision, minimum observation/sample conditions, functional effects and configured breach/recovery signals.

patterns.title: Exercise actual API SDK CLI integration journeys
patterns.problem: Backend examples and error guidance promise an integration path that does not work.
patterns.when_to_use: A changed public API/SDK/CLI setup, example, error or compatibility contract.
patterns.approach: Pin one representative setup-to-success and recovery flow. Execute supported entrypoints in an authorized disposable environment, record starting conditions and distinguish measured, inferred and blocked claims.
failure_modes: Warm environment reported as first-time onboarding
Source-only upgrade review claimed runtime compatible
verification: Execute the documented flow and a safe invalid-input/recovery case; verify effects, diagnostics and the relevant supported invocation.
